subject: physiology
title: Haemostasis: platelets, cascades and fibrinolysis

steps.tx: **Primary haemostasis** clenches vessels in spasm, bridges platelets by von Willebrand factor onto GPIb collagen, recruits by ADP, constricts and aggregates by thromboxane, blocked at cyclo oxygenase by aspirin and at the ADP receptor by clopidogrel. Tests span bleeding time and platelet counts with smears for giants, closure by platelet function analyser, Bernard Soulier giants lacking GPIb and Glanzmann failure to aggregate, while thrombocytopenia from dengue, immune destruction or hypersplenism bleeds from mucosa and skin. Vessels therefore clench before factors knit.
steps.say: A cut vessel first narrows, then platelets stick by von Willebrand factor, activate with ADP and thromboxane, and aggregate into a plug, each step matched to a drug in the diagram. Aspirin blocks thromboxane production, clopidogrel blocks ADP signalling, and missing receptors explain Bernard Soulier and Glanzmann failures. Low counts from immune destruction or sequestration bleed from gums and skin as purpura.

vis.alt: Primary haemostasis: vascular spasm, platelet adhesion by von Willebrand factor binding GPIb to collagen, activation releasing ADP and thromboxane A2, aggregation through GPIIb IIIa and fibrinogen; aspirin blocks thromboxane, clopidogrel blocks the ADP receptor, abciximab blocks GPIIb IIIa.
vis.caption: Adhesion (vWF, GPIb), activation (ADP, TXA2), aggregation (GPIIb/IIIa, fibrinogen); each step has a drug.

steps.tx: The **coagulation cascade** fires extrinsically by tissue factor seven after trauma, intrinsically through twelve, eleven, nine and eight timed by APTT, and commonly through ten, five, two and fibrinogen timed by PT, cross linked by thirteen and carboxylated by vitamin K, prolonged by warfarin. Haemophilia A lacks eight into joints, B lacks nine as Christmas disease, replaced by factor against inhibitors, and von Willebrand disease bleeds mucosally releasing stores by desmopressin, while lupus anticoagulant paradoxically clots.
steps.say: Two laboratory routes converge on factor ten: tissue factor with seven drives the prothrombin time, the contact route drives the partial thromboplastin time, and both build thrombin to knit fibrin cross linked by factor thirteen, mapped in the cascade figure. Vitamin K activates factors two, seven, nine and ten, so warfarin prolongs both times. Missing eight or nine causes joint bleeding haemophilia, von Willebrand disease bleeds from mucosa, and desmopressin can release stored factor.

vis.alt: Coagulation cascade: intrinsic pathway XII XI IX with VIII and extrinsic pathway tissue factor with VIIa both activate X, which with V converts prothrombin to thrombin, converting fibrinogen to fibrin, cross linked by XIII; PT tests the extrinsic route, APTT the intrinsic, and warfarin lowers II VII IX and X.
vis.caption: PT follows the extrinsic pathway (VII) and warfarin; APTT follows the intrinsic pathway and heparin.

steps.tx: **Fibrinolysis** by tissue plasminogen activator makes plasmin digesting fibrin to degradation products and D-dimer, blocked by tranexamic acid, consumed with prolonged bleeding and clotting in disseminated intravascular coagulation, failed by liver lacking factors and replaced as fibrinogen by cryoprecipitate. Anticoagulants span heparin by APTT with thrombocytopenia risk, warfarin by INR and greens, direct agents by renal clearance, reversed by prothrombin complex and idarucizumab, while Virchow thrombosis needs Wells scoring, Doppler and computed tomography for embolism. Clots therefore lyse under control.
steps.say: Formed clot must later dissolve: tissue plasminogen activator frees plasmin to cut fibrin into fragments including D-dimer, the process drawn in the lysis figure that tranexamic acid restrains. Disseminated coagulation consumes factors while clotting, liver failure underproduces them, and cryoprecipitate restores fibrinogen. Heparin, warfarin and direct anticoagulants thin blood by different routes with specific reversals, while venous thrombosis follows Virchow triad to Doppler or scan.

vis.alt: Fibrinolysis: tissue plasminogen activator converts plasminogen to plasmin, which digests fibrin into fibrin degradation products including D-dimer; PAI-1 and alpha-2 antiplasmin inhibit it, and tranexamic acid blocks plasminogen binding.
vis.caption: D-dimer rises when cross-linked fibrin has been broken down: it flags clot formation and lysis.

steps.tx: **Transfusion** gives platelets near ten thousand prophylactically or when bleeding, fresh frozen plasma for INR before procedures, cryoprecipitate for low fibrinogen, febrile allergic TRALI and TACO reactions watched, and massive ratios one to one to one with calcium warmed. Immune thrombocytopenia takes steroids first, immunoglobulin rapidly, splenectomy chronically and romiplostim mimicking thrombopoietin, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura shows a neuro pentad needing daily plasma exchange and caplacizumab against von Willebrand factor, and haemolytic uraemic syndrome after diarrhoea splits away without plasma. Units therefore warm before exchange.
steps.say: Blood components each answer a deficit: platelets near ten thousand, plasma for clotting factors, cryoprecipitate for fibrinogen, and massive bleeding in equal ratios with calcium and warmth. Immune platelet destruction starts with steroids, rises quickly with immunoglobulin, and may need splenectomy or a thrombopoietin mimetic. Thrombotic microangiopathy with brain signs demands urgent plasma exchange, while diarrhoeal haemolytic uraemic syndrome in children follows a different path.
